subject: ILCE-6400 external stock 2.00 recovery failure scenarios

evidence.claim: The analyzed 2.00 receiver is a post-install artifact; the earlier receiver that installs 2.00 has not been identified.

scenarios.blocker: No external entry path independent of the modified normal UI and application runtime has been established.

evidence.claim: The camera-side receiver, authenticity boundary, and failure mapping remain unresolved in the static evidence.

scenarios.blocker: No resume, rollback, atomicity, or independently verified complete-stock rewrite behavior is known after an interrupted feature update.

evidence.claim: The packaged main system follows the normal boot path, while the pre-normal-runtime updater selector remains unidentified.

scenarios.blocker: No independently bootable maintenance or updater entry has been established for a failed application layer.

evidence.claim: Host-side model and version statuses are mapped, but the enforcing camera logic and its acceptance policy remain unknown.

scenarios.blocker: Acceptance of an exact 2.00 reinstall after modification, including same-version or downgrade gates, has not been established.

evidence.claim: The warm-resume path is not an updater selector, and the earlier component that selects the updater system has not been located.

scenarios.blocker: No external recovery entry independent of the affected boot-chain stages and normal application runtime has been established.
Restart, resume, rollback, and safe terminal behavior after power loss during stock restoration are not known.

conclusion: All six mandatory failure scenarios remain unestablished. The exact stock source is authenticated, but static evidence does not establish an external runtime-independent entry, complete write scope, post-write verification, downgrade acceptance, boot-chain recovery, or power-loss safety.
